first.rationale: Aggressive competitor pricing creates the most immediate qualified-revenue threat among price-sensitive SMBs, and prior pricing evidence indicates acquisition and revenue lift. Verify pricing durability and compare against onboarding evidence before committing; use a guarded, targeted test to limit discounting and customer-value risk.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified source record showed completion up 13%, time-to-value down 2.1 days, and 30-day retention up 3%, directly addressing the current 4% onboarding-completion decline while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified revenue lift came with a 12% 30-day retention decline.

final2.rationale: Continue with simplified onboarding rather than switch to promotional pricing. The verified onboarding result improves completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly supporting durable revenue amid falling completion. The only verified pricing evidence produced a 12% 30-day retention decline and does not establish that deeper discounts prevent churn; escalating discounting would risk worsening long-term cohort value despite the acute competitive pressure.
